root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `yr_re_ast_split_at_chaining_point()` treats a large non-greedy `RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY` as a chaining point and enters the split body, that candidate gap node must have both a left sibling and a right sibling in the concat list.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable guard admits the singleton `.{,}?` gap even though both sibling links are NULL, so the split body rewires the original AST around a one-node concat and leaves `re_ast->root_node->children_tail` pointing at the node it will free. The fixed program adds both sibling checks to this decision, so the stock PoC is guarded and only a neighbor-bearing perturbation reaches the split body genuinely.

nodes.state: After the vulnerable split rewiring on the singleton gap, the original AST still carries `re_ast->root_node->children_tail` pointing to the selected `child` even though `children_head` has already been advanced away from it.
The same `child` node left in the original AST tail is then passed to `yr_re_node_destroy(child)`, ending that node's lifetime while the stale tail still aliases it.

`yr_re_ast_extract_literal()` reloads `child` from `re_ast->root_node->children_tail`; the very next `child->type` test in the loop condition is the AddressSanitizer-reported heap-use-after-free read.

edges.relation: The stale original-AST tail aliases the exact `child` pointer that `yr_re_ast_split_at_chaining_point()` immediately frees.
The exact node freed by `yr_re_node_destroy(child)` is later reloaded from the stale `children_tail` field in `yr_re_ast_extract_literal()`, so the sink executes after the free on the same node.
